raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

I hit a CUDA illegal-memory-access error on WSL2 while HiCache was backing up Mamba state to host memory. The stack went through `transfer_kv_mamba_lf_pf` and `submit_device_to_host`; the CUDA watchdog reported the error while flushing pending backups.

I looked at the host pointers on the same RTX 5090 system. The CUDA capability query said registered host memory was supported, but `cudaHostGetDevicePointer` returned a device address different from the host address for a `cudaHostRegister` buffer. With PyTorch-pinned memory, the addresses matched, and a small CUDA kernel write to that buffer worked. This points to a host-pointer compatibility issue on this WSL2 setup, though I have only verified it on this machine.

The relevant setup was a Qwen3.8-family 27B NVFP4 target with a matching DFlash2 NVFP4 draft, FP8 KV cache, and HiCache configured with `page_first`, `write_through_selective`, and the `kernel` I/O backend. The run used ModelOpt FP4 quantization, `--max-total-tokens 175064`, `--max-mamba-cache-size 10`, Mamba `bfloat16` with the `extra_buffer` radix strategy, page size `64`, chunked prefill `4096`, and at most two running requests. At the time, `--mem-fraction-static` was `0.89` and `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_ALLOC` was unset. The original log showed 151,488 KV tokens; the memory fraction was later lowered to `0.78`. Before the fix, I saw the crash with different request contents, so it does not appear to depend on a particular prompt.

The relevant excerpt from the incident log is:

```text
2026-10-09T08:04:03Z INFO: "POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
2026-10-09T08:04:04Z Decode batch, #full token: 19200, Mamba usage: 0.30
2026-10-09T08:04:08Z Prefill batch, #new-token: 4096, Mamba usage: 0.30
2026-10-09T08:04:09Z Prefill batch, #new-token: 4096, Mamba usage: 0.80
2026-10-09T08:04:09Z Process group watchdog: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
2026-10-09T08:04:09Z CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported at some other API call.

File sglang/kernels/ops/mamba/transfer_mamba.py, line 74, in transfer_kv_mamba_lf_pf
File sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/mamba.py, line 587, in _copy_tensor_all_layers_lf_pf
File sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/mamba.py, line 729, in backup_from_device_all_layer
File sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/base.py, line 433, in backup_from_device_all_layer_physical
File sglang/srt/mem_cache/l2_transfer.py, line 136, in submit_device_to_host
File sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py, line 842, in start_writing
```

The `200 OK` is logged before the CUDA error; it does not mean the generation finished successfully. CUDA also warns that errors may surface asynchronously, so this stack identifies the path involved but not necessarily the exact faulting instruction.

## Modifications

When `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_ALLOC=auto` (the default), use PyTorch-pinned host allocations on WSL and keep `cudaHostRegister` on other platforms. `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_ALLOC=pin` and `register` allow users to override the choice.

The pinned allocator needs HiCache pinning enabled and the default host allocator. It raises a clear error for shared-memory or external/custom allocators rather than silently substituting a different allocation strategy. I added unit coverage for the selection logic and these unsupported cases, and documented the setting.

`test_hicache_host_register.py` passed all 19 tests using its `unittest` entry point. Registered-test lint and `git diff --check` passed. Pre-commit formatting and the full code-style checks were not run locally.

On the rebuilt image, the default `auto` setting selected PyTorch pinned memory on the WSL2 kernel. The serving test used `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_ALLOC=pin`. A controlled overlap test ran a 19,199-token prompt that generated 2,048 tokens, then submitted a second 4,099-token prompt 8 seconds later; it generated 128 tokens. Both chat-completion requests returned HTTP 200, the service remained healthy, and the logs contained no CUDA illegal-memory-access error. Mamba usage peaked at 0.60, below the 0.80 shown in the incident log. Since applying the change, I have also been able to run long-chain agent turns normally and have not seen the illegal-memory-access error again. The full project suite and upstream CI have not been run.

The incident log came from Python 3.12 and showed FlashInfer `0.7.0.post1` on SM120. The post-change runtime used PyTorch `2.14.1+cu130`, FlashInfer `0.7.0.post1`, and `sglang-kernel 0.4.9+cu130`. I did not capture the original runtime's immutable image digest or NVIDIA driver version, so these details should not be read as a complete lockfile for the failing run.

## Accuracy Tests

This change only affects host-memory allocation and does not change model computation, so I did not run an accuracy evaluation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance benchmark was run. The post-change checks were focused on allocation and service correctness, not throughput.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

files.patch:
@@ -30,6 +30,18 @@ Notes:
 
 - Besides configuring `--hicache-storage-backend` at startup, SGLang also supports **runtime attach/detach** of the HiCache storage backend (no restart required) via HTTP admin endpoints. See [Runtime Attach/Detach HiCache Storage Backend](./hicache_storage_runtime_attach_detach).
 
+### Host Memory Allocation on WSL2
+
+HiCache normally registers its host buffers with `cudaHostRegister`. On WSL2, some CUDA configurations require buffers allocated with PyTorch's pinned-memory allocator instead. SGLang automatically selects that allocator when it detects a WSL kernel. To override the selection, set `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_ALLOC` before starting the server:
+
+```bash
+export SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_ALLOC=pin       # Use PyTorch pinned host allocations
+# export SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_ALLOC=register # Force cudaHostRegister
+# export SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_ALLOC=auto     # Detect WSL (default)
+```
+
+The `pin` allocator requires pinned HiCache memory and the default host allocator; it is not compatible with shared-memory (`shm`) or external storage allocators. The setting is read when the HiCache host allocator is first selected, so configure it before server startup.
+
 ## Key Configurations with Storage Backends Enabled
 
 ### Memory Layout Optimization

@@ -3,6 +3,7 @@
 import json
 import logging
 import os
+import platform
 from collections import defaultdict
 from functools import lru_cache
 
@@ -322,8 +323,55 @@ def make_kernel_ptr_table(
     )
 
 
+def _alloc_with_pinned_host_memory(
+    dims: tuple,
+    dtype: torch.dtype,
+    device: str,
+    pin_memory: bool,
+    allocator: HostTensorAllocator,
+    registration_granularity_bytes: int | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Use cudaHostAlloc-backed pinned memory where cudaHostRegister is unsafe."""
+    if type(allocator) is not HostTensorAllocator:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_ALLOC=pin requires the default HiCache host "
+            "allocator; mmap/shm and external storage allocators are incompatible."
+        )
+    if not pin_memory:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_ALLOC=pin requires pinned HiCache host memory."
+        )
+    return alloc_with_pin_memory(
+        dims,
+        dtype=dtype,
+        device=device,
+        pin_memory=pin_memory,
+        allocator=None,
+    )
+
+
+def _default_alloc_memory_func():
+    host_alloc = os.getenv("SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_ALLOC", "auto").strip().lower()
+    if host_alloc not in ("auto", "pin", "register"):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_ALLOC must be one of: auto, pin, register; "
+            f"got {host_alloc!r}"
+        )
+    use_pin_memory = host_alloc == "pin" or (
+        host_alloc == "auto" and "microsoft" in platform.uname().release.lower()
+    )
+    if use_pin_memory:
+        logger.warning(
+            "HiCache host allocator: using torch pin_memory (cudaHostAlloc) "
+            "instead of cudaHostRegister; this is required for GPU-direct access "
+            "to pinned host memory on WSL2."
+        )
+        return _alloc_with_pinned_host_memory
+    return alloc_with_host_register
+
+
 ALLOC_MEMORY_FUNCS = defaultdict(
-    lambda: alloc_with_host_register,
+    _default_alloc_memory_func,
     {
         "npu": alloc_with_pin_memory,
         "musa": alloc_with_pin_memory,

@@ -1,3 +1,5 @@
+import os
+import platform
 import unittest
 from types import SimpleNamespace
 from unittest import mock
@@ -10,6 +12,7 @@
     DeepSeekV4PagedHostPool,
     DeepSeekV4StateHostPool,
 )
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.pool_host import common as pool_host_common
 from sglang.srt.mem_cache.pool_host import mha as mha_pool_host
 from sglang.srt.mem_cache.pool_host import mla as mla_pool_host
 from sglang.srt.mem_cache.pool_host.common import (
@@ -66,6 +69,111 @@ def cudaGetErrorString(self, rc: int) -> str:
 
 
 class TestHiCacheHostRegister(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_auto_allocator_uses_pinned_memory_on_wsl2(self):
+        with (
+            mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_ALLOC": "auto"}),
+            mock.patch.object(
+                platform,
+                "uname",
+                return_value=SimpleNamespace(
+                    release="5.15.167-microsoft-standard-WSL2"
+                ),
+            ),
+        ):
+            allocator = pool_host_common._default_alloc_memory_func()
+
+        self.assertIs(allocator, pool_host_common._alloc_with_pinned_host_memory)
+
+    def test_auto_allocator_keeps_host_registration_outside_wsl2(self):
+        with (
+            mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_ALLOC": "auto"}),
+            mock.patch.object(
+                platform,
+                "uname",
+                return_value=SimpleNamespace(release="6.8.0-generic"),
+            ),
+        ):
+            allocator = pool_host_common._default_alloc_memory_func()
+
+        self.assertIs(allocator, pool_host_common.alloc_with_host_register)
+
+    def test_explicit_host_registration_overrides_wsl2_auto_detection(self):
+        with (
+            mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_ALLOC": "register"}),
+            mock.patch.object(
+                platform,
+                "uname",
+                return_value=SimpleNamespace(
+                    release="5.15.167-microsoft-standard-WSL2"
+                ),
+            ),
+        ):
+            allocator = pool_host_common._default_alloc_memory_func()
+
+        self.assertIs(allocator, pool_host_common.alloc_with_host_register)
+
+    def test_explicit_pinned_allocator_overrides_non_wsl2_auto_detection(self):
+        with (
+            mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_ALLOC": "pin"}),
+            mock.patch.object(
+                platform,
+                "uname",
+                return_value=SimpleNamespace(release="6.8.0-generic"),
+            ),
+        ):
+            allocator = pool_host_common._default_alloc_memory_func()
+
+        self.assertIs(allocator, pool_host_common._alloc_with_pinned_host_memory)
+
+    def test_invalid_host_allocator_setting_is_rejected(self):
+        with (
+            mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_ALLOC": "unknown"}),
+            self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "auto, pin, register"),
+        ):
+            pool_host_common._default_alloc_memory_func()
+
+    def test_pinned_allocator_uses_torch_pinned_allocation(self):
+        tensor = object()
+        with mock.patch.object(
+            pool_host_common, "alloc_with_pin_memory", return_value=tensor
+        ) as alloc:
+            result = pool_host_common._alloc_with_pinned_host_memory(
+                (4, 8),
+                dtype=torch.float16,
+                device="cpu",
+                pin_memory=True,
+                allocator=pool_host_common.HostTensorAllocator(),
+            )
+
+        self.assertIs(result, tensor)
+        alloc.assert_called_once_with(
+            (4, 8),
+            dtype=torch.float16,
+            device="cpu",
+            pin_memory=True,
+            allocator=None,
+        )
+
+    def test_pinned_allocator_rejects_non_default_storage_allocator(self):
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "mmap/shm and external"):
+            pool_host_common._alloc_with_pinned_host_memory(
+                (4, 8),
+                dtype=torch.float16,
+                device="cpu",
+                pin_memory=True,
+                allocator=object(),
+            )
+
+    def test_pinned_allocator_requires_pin_memory(self):
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "requires pinned HiCache"):
+            pool_host_common._alloc_with_pinned_host_memory(
+                (4, 8),
+                dtype=torch.float16,
+                device="cpu",
+                pin_memory=False,
+                allocator=pool_host_common.HostTensorAllocator(),
+            )
+
     def test_dsa_page_layouts_with_draft_use_page_registration_granularity(self):
         target_buffers = [torch.empty(1, dtype=torch.uint8) for _ in range(3)]
         draft_buffer = torch.empty(1, dtype=torch.uint8)
